articles.authors: Yuntian Guo, Tianye Zheng, Feng Shi, Junbo Li, Yuan Wang, Guoming Ma, Hao Feng Zhao
articles.summary: Ni-rich NCM811 cathode is critical for achieving high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) but its instability issue at high potentials vs Li/Li+ remains unresolved. Mechanical degradation and lattice oxygen release of NCM811 could trigger nonequilibrium interfacial side reactions, including electrolyte oxidation, interphase evolution, and impedance growth. Understanding these processes is essential for the rational design of stable high-voltage electrolytes compatible with NCM811 cathodes. …

articles.title: FTIR-Based Quantification of a Corrosion Inhibitor in Solution: Experimental Investigation and Quantum-Chemical Modeling
articles.authors: Zimmer H, Andreeva N, Chaban V, Bernard F, da Costa E
institutions: Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul
Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University
articles.summary: Residual corrosion inhibitor (RCI) monitoring is essential for ensuring the effectiveness of corrosion mitigation programs in oil and gas production systems. Among the available analytical techniques, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) offers advantages such as rapid analysis, minimal sample preparation, and the absence of chemical reagents. In this study, an FTIR-based method was developed for the quantification of 2-phenyl-2-imidazoline (IMDZ), a corrosion inhibitor, and the influence of typical produced-water constituents on its spectroscopic response was investigated. Calibration curves were constructed using IMDZ concentrations ranging from 100 to 1000 ppm in Milli-Q water. …

articles.title: Mapping Site-Specific Water Uptake and Transport in Covalent Organic Frameworks through Molecular Dynamics and In Situ Vibrational Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Tsukasa Irie, Sairathna Choppella, Yasukaze Nishimura, Tokuhisa Kawawaki, Hitoshi Washizu, Yuka Ikemoto, Mahesh Kumar Ravva, Saikat Chandra Das, Yuichi Negishi
articles.summary: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is governed by pore chemistry and confinement, yet the molecular origins of uptake and mobility remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate site-specific water adsorption and transport in two structurally related COFs, TUS-46 and TUS-44, by combining molecular dynamics simulations with humidity-controlled in situ FT-IR spectroscopy. TUS-46 exhibits accelerated pore filling and enhanced hydration through cooperative hydrogen-bond formation, whereas stronger water−framework interactions constrain translational mobility, revealing an affinity−mobility decoupling. …

articles.summary: Dyslipidemias are abnormalities in lipid metabolism associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. This study evaluated Raman spectroscopy as an alternative to spectrophotometry for the analysis of total cholesterol. Serum samples from volunteers and a control serum sample were analyzed. The samples were analyzed by spectrophotometry and subjected to spectroscopic analysis using a dispersive Raman spectrometer (830 nm, 350 mW, 30 s). The spectra obtained were compared to the Raman spectra of an authentic total cholesterol standard. …

institutions: Clinical Oncology School of Fujian Medical University
articles.summary: A surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) biochip integrating CRISPR/Cas12a with catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) was developed for the ultrasensitive and precise quantification of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) harbouring non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) associated mutations. Upon hybridization with target ctDNA, the CHA circuit generates abundant H1−H2 duplexes, which efficiently activate the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a. The activated Cas12a indiscriminately cleaves linker single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), thereby disrupting the programmed self-assembly of SERS nanoprobes (Au@MBN@Ag NPs) on a two-dimensional Ag-coated silicon substrate. …

articles.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
articles.summary: Phenylketonuria is associated with elevated levels of l-phenylalanine (l-Phe), which can self-assemble into amyloid-like fibrillar aggregates at pathological concentrations. Upon lowering the solution pH to 1.5, protonation of l-Phe induces a morphology transition from fibrillar assemblies to flake-like aggregates, as confirmed by optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), owing to enhanced electrostatic repulsion among the molecules. However, the influence of such morphology-dependent self-assembled structures on membrane organization remains poorly understood. …

articles.summary: Controlling the fate of photoexcited carriers at semiconductor surfaces is a central problem connecting ultrafast materials science with infrared detection, high-speed optoelectronics, and quantum-device engineering. Yet carrier lifetimes are commonly reported as intrinsic material constants. In narrow-gap InAs, surface Fermi-level pinning creates an electron accumulation layer with quantized subbands, so the measured lifetime may depend on how carriers are prepared and observed. …

articles.summary: The spin-wave frequency hysteresis loop induced by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in an epitaxial ultrathin Pt/Re/Co/Pt layer studied by Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy (BLS) is presented. The Co thickness of 2 nm is below the exchange length, ensuring in-depth homogeneous magnetization. Static characterization confirms the system resides in the easy-plane magnetic anisotropy regime with quality factor Q < 1. …

articles.authors: Zhaoqi Yi, Xueying Yang, Qing Han, Xiaohu Wu, Yi Wang, Yiqun Zheng
articles.summary: Gold nanoplates (Au NPs) exhibit strong localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) in the near-infrared region, yet precisely aligning their principal absorption band with laser wavelengths in the NIR-I (e.g., 808 nm) or NIR-II (e.g., 1064 nm) biological window remains a critical challenge for effective photothermal therapy. Herein, we demonstrate a facile thermal annealing strategy that enables programmable LSPR tuning of Au nanoplates across both NIR-I and NIR-II regions through thermally induced morphological deformation. …

articles.summary: Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is an unparalleled technique for probing local structural and spectroscopic information at the atomic scale. However, the spectral resolution of conventional STEM-EELS is primarily limited by the intrinsic energy spread of electron sources, making it difficult to capture ultra-low energy-loss signatures, particularly lattice vibrations in the energy-loss range of milli-electron-volt (meV). …

articles.summary: Layered double hydroxides, as a class of 2D van der Waals hybrids, are generally regarded as non-polar due to their centrosymmetric crystal structures, despite their highly tunable compositions and interlayer chemistries. Their functional modulation has largely relied on surface modification, defect engineering, or composite formation. Here, we report a coordination-driven route to intrinsic piezoelectricity in a carbonate-intercalated 2D van der Waals hybrid enabled by controlled yttrium (Y 3+ ) substitution within metal hydroxide layers. …
